clinicalPearls: Caused by mutations in MPZ, which encodes myelin protein zero (P0), the most abundant structural protein of peripheral myelin; inheritance is autosomal dominant.
Shows a characteristically bimodal phenotype: a severe early-onset (infantile, Dejerine-Sottas-like) form and a milder late-onset form.
The early-onset form has very slow conduction velocities and delayed motor milestones, whereas the late-onset form often behaves like an axonal neuropathy with relatively preserved velocities.
The mutation itself largely predicts the phenotype, so genotype-phenotype correlation is unusually informative in this subtype.
Some MPZ mutations are associated with distinctive extra features such as tonic (Adie-like) pupils and sensorineural hearing loss.
Less common than CMT1A but an important cause of both demyelinating and later axonal-appearing hereditary neuropathy.
Diagnosis rests on MPZ sequencing, typically pursued when the PMP22 duplication is negative.
reference.pathophysiology: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B is caused by mutations in MPZ, which encodes myelin protein zero (P0), the principal structural glycoprotein of peripheral myelin, where it mediates adhesion and compaction of adjacent myelin membrane layers. The consequences are strongly mutation-specific: some variants cause protein misfolding or a toxic gain of function that severely disrupts myelin from infancy and produces very slow conduction, whereas others act largely through loss of function, giving a later-onset, more axonal phenotype with relatively preserved conduction velocities. This mechanistic split underlies the characteristic bimodal clinical spectrum. Pathology shows segmental demyelination and remyelination and, in early-onset disease, uncompacted or poorly formed myelin, with secondary axonal loss driving long-term disability. Inheritance is autosomal dominant.
additionalDifferentials: CMT1A (PMP22 duplication), the commonest demyelinating CMT
CMT2 subtypes, particularly when late-onset CMT1B appears axonal
Dejerine-Sottas or congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy at the severe end
Other MPZ-related phenotypes within the same gene
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies (markedly slow in early-onset, near-normal or axonal in late-onset disease)
Ophthalmology review for pupillary abnormalities where suspected
Audiology if hearing symptoms are present
Family segregation studies and genetic counselling
Nerve biopsy in atypical cases (onion bulbs or uncompacted myelin)
redFlags: Infantile hypotonia and markedly delayed walking indicating the severe early-onset form
Superimposed inflammatory features raising the possibility of a treatable acquired neuropathy
Prominent pupillary or auditory involvement pointing specifically to MPZ
reference.prognosis: The course is highly variable: early-onset severe forms cause substantial childhood disability, whereas late-onset forms progress slowly through adulthood with a normal lifespan.
pitfalls: Assuming CMT1B is always demyelinating, when late-onset disease can look axonal and mimic CMT2.
Missing the pupillary or auditory clues that point specifically to an MPZ cause.
Failing to test MPZ in a demyelinating neuropathy once the PMP22 duplication is negative.
Overlooking the strong genotype-phenotype relationship when counselling families.
management: Base care on supportive management, as no disease-modifying therapy exists, with physiotherapy and occupational therapy tailored to disease severity
Provide ankle-foot orthoses, podiatry, footwear and walking aids for foot drop, pes cavus and hammer toes
In severe early-onset Dejerine-Sottas-like disease provide intensive paediatric rehabilitation and developmental support, and offer foot surgery for disabling deformity in milder late-onset disease
Treat neuropathic pain symptomatically and avoid neurotoxic drugs such as vincristine
Screen for the MPZ-associated features of tonic pupils and sensorineural hearing loss with ophthalmology and audiology assessment
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance, using genotype-phenotype correlation to guide prognosis, and assess relatives
Coordinate multidisciplinary neuromuscular, orthopaedic, audiology and rehabilitation care
